bluf: DEPT is an Amsterdam based network agency of 4,000+ people, backed by The Carlyle Group, selling itself as a Growth Invention company that leads with AI transformation: DEPTIFY agentic orchestration, ADA/DASH headless builds and a 400+ person DEPT/AI unit. The record shows it moving up the stack, from a Gartner 2026 Magic Quadrant Leader rating and $4B media under management toward agentic engineering and GEO audits. The one thing a rival should know: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, and 14 of its 19 named clients are names only. It is very likely, with high confidence, the reference bidder on enterprise AI transformation briefs in Europe.
doing:
The positioning line, in the record's words: a self styled Growth Invention company, split evenly between tech and marketing, partner led, helping ambitious brands grow faster through AI, experience and media. In plain words, a holdco scale network that wants to be bought as a technology consultancy and sells through platform partnerships. The headline claim pairs a Gartner Leader rating in the 2026 Magic Quadrant with $4B of media under management; the about page adds 30+ offices on five continents and 30 acquisitions since 2015.

Two lines lead at score 3: AI Automation / Agents (DEPTIFY agentic orchestration and four AI transformation consulting offers on the homepage) and Web & Product (the ADA/DASH headless accelerator, with Brookfield Zoo and ENGIE Sitecore builds). Four core lines sit at score 2: AI Search / GEO (a GEO discoverability audit, a case readying a fintech for AI search), Creator & Influencer (creator led trust, an influencer campaign, a social first docuseries, Palfinger storytelling), Data & Measurement (analytics, BI, data and AI governance, the smart Adobe Journey Optimizer case) and SEO (technical SEO, schema and indexing, an SEO migration case). Proprietary: DEPTIFY, ADA/DASH, ADA/DEPT and the Growth Invention Flywheel. Partners: Adobe, Google, Optimizely, Salesforce and Shopify. Paid Search, Paid Social, Programmatic & CTV and Retail Media score only 1.

The AI posture is the lead, not a bolt on: agentic engineering, future of work consulting, GEO audits and the DEPT/AI unit, with cases dated 2026-07-10 (agentic AI and MCP) and 2026-08-17 (an AI ready discovery engine on an Adobe website).

Moves in date order: 2020-01, The Carlyle Group became its backer; 2025, repositioned as the Growth Invention Company at its 10th anniversary (year inferred); 2026, rated a Leader by Gartner. No news, no jobs and no pricing signals are listed (P5 unknown). Conspicuously absent for a network claiming $4B of media: no paid or retail media line scores above 1.
clients:
The client type is enterprise; verticals listed are retail and commerce, tech, media and telecom, consumer packaged goods, banking, financial services and insurance, health, automotive, travel and fashion; the home market is Europe from an HQ in Amsterdam, with offices across the Netherlands, DACH, the Nordics, UK & Ireland, Latin America, India and Australia & Oceania.

The book holds 19 names, 5 with an observed need and 14 names only. Observed: Patagonia (commerce and marketplaces, a branded commerce experience), Pelican (commerce, a legacy turned into a D2C ecommerce store), Palfinger (brand and creative plus social and creators, social first storytelling), Riot Games (brand and creative, design for a mid season invitational) and ENGIE (web build and platform, a new Sitecore platform). The mix read: commerce 0.449, brand 0.315, web 0.157, social 0.079.

Names only: NVIDIA, eBay (title: Turning nothing to wear into something with eBay UK), Meta, Arm (signal: Connecting banks with sustainable farming through Acorn), Just Eat Takeaway.com, Google, Brookfield Zoo Chicago and WHOOP (read as named only despite titles naming a web experience), smart, H&Mbeyond (H&M Group), Geiger (the one press release), Paula's Choice, Kali Healthcare and JYSK; for these the need is inferred from what DEPT leads with, web build and AI and automation first.

Shared: Google on huge, instrument, r-ga, media-monks, akqa and brave-bison; eBay on mindgruve; Meta on media-monks; 3 shared of 19.

What the base needs next: with KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer) the strongest tailwind, it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the commerce names (Patagonia, Pelican, JYSK, eBay) come back for feeds, entities and agentic checkout readiness, and a roughly even chance that the brand and social names (Palfinger, Riot Games) meet the KJ5 price split on paid social and programmatic.
house: Say and do: 2 of 3 tested lines hold. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while its sitemap holds 74 AI topic URLs, the one gap the Radar flags. Publishing cadence is corroborated, 6 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 8 in 365, on a sitemap of 10,071 URLs. Creator & Influencer is corroborated by its own instagram and tiktok channels linked from the site. It blocks no AI crawlers. The stack is gtm and usercentrics on WordPress; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack detected. Google ads: 8 on record, 0 in the last 30 days, 3 text and 5 video, advertiser DEPT Holding BV, last shown 2026-06-18. LinkedIn: 19 company ads, 0 thought leader ads, a floor since 2,053 ads match the name query; one sample reads 'How much friction is hiding in your daily tech stack? Too often, tools, data, and AI operate in silos'.
market:
The Horus read: tailwind index 25.3, band Favored, 82nd percentile, integrity 66.7. Best placed for KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net 0.306), driven by Data & Measurement at +2 and AI Automation / Agents at +1, and for KJ1 (The click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.175) on AI Search / GEO at +2. Most exposed to KJ5 (The price of attention splits in two, net -0.068) through Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV. Best fit: The Bazaar of Agents at 45/100. P moves: making P1 and P2; partial on P6 and P7; absent on P8; unknown on P5; P3 and P4 not applicable.

The Monsoon read: index 62.2, band Onshore wind, 75th percentile, migration 77.2 against displacement 47.2. The verdict puts 52 of the index on the sold mix, Web & Product (14) and SEO (9) carrying the most movable hours, and sends 56% of the work to South and Southeast Asia and 35% to Eastern Europe. The class is observed: a delivery footprint in India is listed, with no onshore claim.
openings:
The contradiction to lead with is observed: DEPT sells AI Search / GEO with a discoverability audit and 74 AI topic URLs, and publishes no llms.txt. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival who shows an enterprise prospect DEPT's own house against its GEO pitch wins the audit conversation, since the Horus read already credits DEPT with P1 and P2 the house is the only soft spot on that line. The falsifier: an llms.txt at dept.global before the next compile.

Price is the second opening. No public pricing model shows (P5 unknown), the Monsoon migration read is 77.2 and a delivery footprint is observed in India: an onshore delivery pitch has something concrete to point at, and a transparent, outcome priced offer has a roughly even chance of drawing an enterprise buyer into a conversation DEPT cannot have in public.

Third, the book: 14 of 19 names are names only, and Google sits on huge, instrument, r-ga, media-monks, akqa and brave-bison; eBay and Meta shop too. Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV score 1, drive its only headwind, KJ5, and P8 is absent. A rival is unlikely to beat it on AI transformation or web build.
watch: I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV would strengthen the KJ4 tailwind DEPT is best placed for, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, while growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and feeds its KJ1 tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would touch its creator and social line under KJ8.
The 2025 repositioning as the Growth Invention Company is the dated move to follow up: whether the 2026 Gartner Leader rating turns into named AI transformation wins on the record.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients, and this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
